newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-NYMEX crude, products to continue uptrend.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-NYMEX crude, products to continue uptrend.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
* NYMEX crude retreated from $20.50 but remains within uptrend. The danger increases if it fails to close above $20 today.
* A key level to be broken for the market to get any higher is $20.65.
NYMEX crude and products look technicaly set to continue in an uptrend on Friday with momentum indicators moving back into neutral and resistance limited.
Analysts said there are few bearish technical signals in the market with both crude and products stabilising after Thursday's volatile session stirred by the August unleaded contract expiry.

They said only the resumption of Iraqi oil sales and profit taking after the recent rally could tip the balance but any correction would be short term with trendline support looking sturdy even if bull sentiment has waned a little recently.
Leslie Nicholas at GNI Research said, "Without a clear lead from gasoline, some of the bulls might feel a little nervous about much higher numbers especially with specific fundamental news looming."
"(NYMEX crude) retreated from $20.50 (on Thursday) but remains within it's uptrend for now. The danger increases if it fails to close above psychological $20 today," Nicholas added.
Fenella Graham at MeesPierson said, "The only caution on the down side would be further worries from Iraq and Friday profit taking."

The NYMEX crude spot month continuation chart saw price action dip below the key $20 figure after breaching resistance at $20.45 on Thursday but the market was looking well supported around the $19.95-$20 range in ACCESS trade.

Omar Gadsby analyst at MCM in London said, "I was a bit disappointed at the lack of follow through strength after the market broke through $20.45. I expect the market to trade choppily sideways in the $19.65-$20.50 range over the next couple of days".
He said there were still some key levels to be broken for the market to get any higher citing the $20.65 level.
That represents a 62 percent Fibonacci retracement of the range between from May 16's $22 high and July 15s $18.50 low, as an important upside marker.

On the September chart slow stochastics crossed at around 65 percent and Thursdays price action formed a reversal pattern, known as a 'hanging man' by analysts who follow Japanese candlestick charting techniques.

However, analysts said the reversal pattern needs the confirmation of a bearish pattern today and said that it along with the stochastics cross could just be flagging a short term correction that a bout of Friday profit taking could bring.

As a result of the August contract expiry and it's backwardation to September of around five cents at the close, unleaded gasoline opened a wide gap on the spot month continuation chart, but the September contract remained well above the uptrend support line established over the recent rally from June 23's 54.85 cent low.

On the September chart price action in ACCESS trading was slightly softer. But again the market was well above long tern uptrend support with a second shorter term line of support from July 21's 56.75 cent low that comes in around 62.40 cents today also underpinning the market.
To the upside Thursday's 63.45 cent high is the initial target.

Heating oil was making headway in ACCESS trading showing little of the softer sentiment of the other markets and continuing an uptrend started from July 18's 51.80 cent low on that keeps it on path to tackle May 16's 58.90 cent high.
RSIs are back in neutral territory and slow stochastic lines look likely to stay apart, leaving room for the market to move higher.
Al Graham at Elliott Wave International said "Look for a near term breach of 56.60 resistance but movement beyond this level should be quite limited".
-- Colin Wooster, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7456
